findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the hero's lead, about 40 words, still sits on the photo. At 390 px it runs five centred lines straight under the two-line H1, almost touching the 'g' of 'Blog', and fills the whole 275 px frame; at 1440 px it fills the band under the title too. The photo shows only as a dark texture behind text.
findings.reference: The competitor's matching page puts only its bold title on the photo, with no lead, and starts its running text on white under the photo band.
findings.fix: Apply the template's rule that a hero lead much longer than the competitor's stands under the hero: render .page-hero__lead under the banner, on white, as the page's lead, and keep only the H1 on the photo (the heroText.leadWords limit should keep a 40-word lead off the photo).

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the three plain sections after the hero (overview, overview-steps, table-1) all sit on white one under the other, at both widths, so only padding separates them.
findings.reference: The site's rule, which follows the competitor's banded pages, is that neighbouring plain sections alternate white and tinted backgrounds.
findings.fix: The template should alternate the plain sections' backgrounds so that overview-steps, between the white overview and the white table-1, takes var(--section-tint).

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the process section has no heading. Its left column holds only the small bold line 'Quality checks at every stage of an order.' beside the five steps, between H2 sections above and below, and leaves a wide empty column (at 390 px the line reads as a stray caption).
findings.reference: The competitor's process lists always open with an H2 above their lead, in the left column beside the steps.
findings.fix: Site Factory should give the overview-steps visual (blog page copy) a heading, for example 'Quality Checks at Every Stage', so the block renders an H2 above the caption line.

findings.issue: The manifest measures the hero H1 as start-aligned and the lead under it as centred, so the heading and text of one block are not aligned the same way.
findings.reference: The competitor's hero title and any text on it share one alignment.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give .page-hero__lead the same text-align as the hero H1 (.page-hero h1) at desktop widths (this goes away if the lead moves under the hero, as the finding above asks).

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the manifest measures the H1 as centred and the lead under it as start-aligned at 390 px, so the heading and text of the hero do not share an alignment.
findings.reference: The competitor's hero title and any text on it share one alignment.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give .page-hero__lead the same text-align as the hero H1 at the mobile breakpoint (this goes away if the lead moves under the hero).

findings.issue: At 390 px the hero is a 275 px band cut from a wide photo, so the photo barely reads behind its text, while the competitor's phone hero is a tall portrait photo that fills most of the first screen.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero shows its factory photo as a tall portrait frame (about 550 px at 390 px wide) with only the title over it.
findings.fix: Let the hero take a portrait crop or a separate portrait photo on phones (art direction per breakpoint) instead of stretching the wide photo's frame, which would cut the photo away.

findings.issue: Each of the ten cards repeats the same grey sub-label 'What this means for you' between its title and its text, so the line adds no information and makes the set read as boilerplate (at 390 px it adds ten more lines to a 3,100 px stack).
findings.reference: The competitor's outlined cards carry only a title and its text, with no repeated label.
findings.fix: Site Factory should drop the repeated 'What this means for you' column label from the table-1 rows, or give each row its own short line, so each card shows its title and then its text.
